The corpus holds only about 13 Vera items and four are narration about her, so the bar set is thinner than ours; it still wins. (a) Voice: ours. Cover the names and Maximilian is identifiable by shape alone: no contractions, 'I shall', 'Do...', a fragment verdict then a procedural ruling. Vera's corpus lines include quest-hook filler ('Come on, think of something!') that any Monster Prom character could say. But his consistency has turned into monotony: most of the bank is the same two beats, '[verdict or observation]. [hotel ruling].' Vera has four shapes (complaint as boast, presumption with 'Right?', the repeated-word fake-out, the one-word order). (b) Construction: bar. His best lines are as tight as hers and turn on the last words. But Vera's status move works at murder scale ('cover up the literal murder... no questions asked'), while most of his presumptions are small: carpets, towels, a board downstairs, a lonely chef. His four or five best lines are exactly the ones where the presumption gets big (most hotels, a bishop mid-sentence, a sunset sent back, the room removed). Around a dozen lines explain their own joke ('That is you', 'That is unheard of', 'How odd', 'We call that a vacancy'). (c) Quotable: tie. 'Put the fee on his room. Then remove the room.' and 'And its parents.' would clip as well as 'my career on not dating losers like you'; past the top five, his set drops faster than hers. Verdict: the bar is the better-written character tonight, because ours does not match it on construction. GENERIC COUNT: 85 of 191 (45%), down from round 1's 48%.
